Whitespace a person types reaches a document from the CLI as a character reference: a spec whose option line ends ' ' gives the item a trailing space, and 'gRPC : Adds streaming' gives it a space before the separator the parse cuts at. That is how the proof made the state the finding is about.

api's TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves refuses this pod's Postgres, whose default collation is byte order, and says so itself. It is the environment, not a failure.
deviations: None of the round's design changed. The drop and the rewrite are now weighed by whether a node writes more than the text in it, which is the rule the empty-question guard already used, so the three checks of this pull request read the same way.

The refusal of a drop and of a rewrite is built from the merge's own result, so the write and the refusal cannot disagree; the order of the two refusals is unchanged, a rewrite before a drop, and the whole edit is refused on the first of either.
discoveredComplexity: pmdoc.WriteBudget charges elements only through a parse (ParseFragment), and RefusePlainText weighs plain letters at nothing, so charging the caller's items to the write's budget means parsing them on it: editedOptionList now parses twice, the caller's own items on the write's budget and the merged list on a budget of its own, which is why both parses exist.

The round-2 reviewed head refuses an edit whose line differs from the trimmed option only by whitespace, and the refusal quotes the whitespace as ' ', so the agent reading it cannot tell what it is being refused for. That is why the fix compares a node with what its own text writes rather than with a node built from the parsed option.
